draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Varkala! This is one of the few places in Kerala where red cliffs meet the sea. Natural springs trickle out of the rock right onto the beach.
draft.hungryLine: The cliff is lined with cafés serving fresh fish, pancakes and everything between. Here's a start.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk the North Cliff path from end to end, then take the steps down to the beach.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Pick a cliff-top café, order a fresh juice and watch the sun drop into the sea.
moodReplies.surprise-me: People believe a dip at Papanasam beach washes away your sins. That's what the name means.

legends.title: The beach that washes sins
legends.body: Hindus come to this beach to perform rites for their ancestors. The name Papanasam means 'destroyer of sins'.

legends.title: A gift from a grateful captain
legends.body: People say the bell at Janardhana Swamy Temple came from a Dutch ship. Its captain gave it after he was saved from a storm.

tips.title: Swim near the lifeguard flags.
tips.body: The currents here can be strong.

tips.title: Compare café menus.
tips.body: Prices on the cliff vary a lot between neighbours.

story.title: A cliff by the sea
story.body: These red laterite cliffs are rare on Kerala's flat coast. Springs seep out of them onto the sand below.

story.title: Pilgrims come
story.body: Janardhana Swamy Temple drew pilgrims to Varkala long before tourists did. Its beach became a place for rituals for ancestors.

story.title: A guru settles
story.body: Sree Narayana Guru, the great social reformer, founded Sivagiri Mutt here. His samadhi is still visited by thousands.

story.title: Travellers find the cliff
story.body: Backpackers found Varkala's quiet cliff, and cafés slowly lined the edge.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Walk the cliff at sunset, then find dinner with a sea view. Tell me which café you'd come back to.
